items.title: Peter LaCaze Interview, 1972-01-27
items.q: INTERVIEWER: ...other than Harrison Bond? Harrison Bond, yeah. ... [INTERVIEWEE] Yeah, Solomon was coming that door, yeah? ... I don't know that name at all. I don't know that name.

ctx.x: Well, Hippolyte Chong. Oh, and I know him real good, too. He was a trumpet player, too. Yeah, he was sick, he got heart trouble, and he had a good plan. Yeah, I knew him good, too. And Sam and Henri Dutry. Oh, I know them good. I used to visit their home, Sam and Henri. Where did they live? Well, at that time, Sam had a pressing business on Anthony and Magazine, and they used to, the brothers used to be there kind of regular, you know, Henri and Peter there, and Sam. I used to go over there. You didn't work with…

Yeah, he played way up until he died. Yeah. I read about a fellow named Duriam in a book. Did you ever hear of anybody called Duriam that played trombone? Duriam? No. Who was the trombone player with the Nola band then, other than Harrison Bond? Harrison Bond, yeah. Anybody else? No, I believe Harrison is the only one.

Yeah, Solomon was coming that door, yeah? All right. He left it open? No, he didn't open. Okay. Well, we can get it. Yeah. Well, I saw in a book about Duriam, and I never heard of anybody. I don't know that name at all. I don't know that name.
